Quick triage notes (engineer on call):
- Observed 503s originating from the dedicated serving pool assigned to Avalon (pool-id: ded-avalon-031).
- Burst budget meter for that pool hit a hard threshold due to a sudden traffic spike; the burst policy then throttled new token allocations while the token-bucket refill logic lagged because of an unexpected sequence-length distribution (longer sequences consumed more tokens per request).
- Additionally, we have a legacy abuse-detection rule that groups similar-but-not-identical X-Client-Id headers and treats them as a single noisy actor; Avalon is rotating client ids across edge nodes which trip that grouping rule. The grouping pushed the effective request rate above the configured per-actor cap.

Immediate mitigation I recommend (low-risk):
1) Emergency override: temporarily relax the burst cap for ded-avalon-031 to allow +60% burst for the next 2 hours.
2) Add a short-term exception to the actor grouping rule for Avalon (whitelist the X-Client-Id pattern).
3) Rotate a routing rule hotfix to better account for sequence-length token accounting (will take ~40 minutes to stage and roll).

I can run steps 1 and 2 now if leadership/ACCT OKs it — impact is increased cost for the hour window but avoids failures.

Logs referenced: INF-4821 (internal), attached trace matches the token-dip pattern.

— Sergio
SRE, Redwood Inference
